subject: Embedding migration follow-up: dims, auth & routing checklist
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir.shah@acmeretail.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Julia Park <julia.park@acmeretail.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up from demo — current embeddings export + questions

Hi Vanessa / Ben,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier today. Julia and I chatted after the call and we pulled the current embedding export to give you better context. Attaching the CSV (acme_embed_export_1536.csv) — vectors are 1536-dimension, normalized with L2 on our side today.

A few follow-ups we hope you can clarify before our next sync:
- Will Redwood accept 1536 vectors as-is or should we re-index into a different dimensionality?
- Any recommended batch sizes / throughput guidance for bulk-migration? We have ~120M vectors.
- Auth: we currently push vectors to vendor APIs via long-lived API keys. For production we want short-lived creds / mTLS. What options does Redwood support for hosted vs private?
- Routing/Failover: we need deterministic fallback if the primary embedding model is overloaded. Do you support model tags / routing by latency SLA?
- Reranker: we currently do an in-house rerank pass. Curious whether Redwood recommends using your hosted reranker or keeping a lightweight on-prem reranker.

Next meeting: Julia and I are available on Friday 10–12 PDT.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Shah
Head of Search & Personalization
Acme Retail

Attachments: acme_embed_export_1536.csv (text/csv, 120MB)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@acmeretail.com>, Julia Park <julia.park@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 18:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — current embeddings export + questions

Hi Samir / Julia — great meeting earlier and thanks for the CSV. High-level answers below, plus proposed next steps and a short mutual action plan.

Quick answers (details / engineering follow-up in the next email):
- Dimensionality: We can accept 1536 vectors as-is. If you want to move to a different dimension (e.g., 768) we recommend either: 1) re-encode with the new model, or 2) store both representations during a phased migration and run hybrid queries. We do not recommend lossy projection unless you can validate recall/precision on your eval set.
- Batching: For bulk ingest we commonly recommend 64–256 vectors per batch depending on instance memory and network MTU. We’ll provide a throughput estimate given your 120M vectors.
- Auth: Hosted: short-lived tokens + scoped API keys; Private: mTLS + KMS-backed signing is available. We'll provide SDK examples for both.
- Routing/failover: Yes — you can set routing policies by latency threshold, region, or customer-tier. We also support automatic fallback to a compatible model variant (e.g., reduced-dim or quantized variant) if capacity is constrained.
- Reranker: Both are supported. Hosted reranker simplifies ops and provides tracing in Console; on-prem reranker reduces egress but requires you to maintain model weights. We can pilot hosted rerank for a subset of queries.

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan):
1) Engineering QA call — deep-dive on dimensions, indexing, and auth (Ben + Karthik).
2) Migration pilot — 5M vectors: ingest, index, run A/B recall vs current system.
3) Rollout plan — store dual representations during pilot, evaluate cost and latency, then choose re-encode vs keep both.

Can you confirm Friday 11:00 PDT for the engineering QA call? I’ll send an invite and include: Ben Carter (sales), Karthik Iyer (platform eng), and Evelyn Hart (solutions manager) to align on timelines and approval steps.

Attachments: redwood-embed-options.pdf (overview)

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: ACME pilot scope — tech clarifications and recommended migration approach

Team,

Following Samir’s ask (see thread), here's the recommended technical plan and open questions for the engineering QA. Please review and flag anything missing.

Summary of constraints from Acme:
- ~120M vectors currently at 1536 dims, L2-normalized, stored in their house index.
- They want minimal downtime and the ability to compare recall vs current system.
- Security: will require short-lived creds in hosted, strong mTLS/KMS in private deployment.

Recommended approach (phased):
A) Pilot ingest (5M vectors) into Redwood hosted for speed:
  - Accept 1536d as-is. Index using HNSW with PQ candidate re-ranking; store payload for reference.
  - Batch config: start with 128 vectors per request; scale to 256 if memory allows. Monitor CPU/GPU utilization and GC.
  - Normalization: continue storing L2-normalized vectors. For recall comparisons run cosine similarity (equivalent after L2).
  - Reranker: run Redwood hosted lightweight cross-encoder for the top-100 candidates. Provide option to send only candidate IDs back to Acme for on-prem rerank if they prefer.

B) Dual-store phase (parallel indexing):
  - Store both legacy 1536 and new 768 (if they plan to re-encode). This lets them A/B without immediate re-encode cost.
  - If re-encoding, recommend validating on their labeled eval set; do not use PCA projection unless validated.

C) Auth & routing:
  - Hosted: issue short-lived scoped tokens via the Redwood Console/SDK. Recommend token TTL = 1 hour for ingestion workflow, rotate keys via KMS.
  - Private/VPC: require mTLS between their ingestion service and the Redwood gateway; Redwood will integrate with their KMS for key rotation and provide audit logs.
  - Routing: configure policy: region -> latency threshold -> model-variant fallback. We'll add a secondary quantized variant for capacity savings.

D) Operational guardrails & costs:
  - Estimate: ingest 5M vectors (128 batch) => ~39K requests; network egress, indexing time, and storage cost estimates attached (embed-migration-costs.xlsx).
  - Monitoring: per-route token-level latency, indexing queue depth, and recall regression alert tied to their evaluation set.

Open engineering questions for the QA call:
- Do they want real-time incremental sync or bulk-only migration window?
- Are there per-vector metadata fields we need to preserve that must be searchable? If so, include in payload mapping.
- Their current reranker is a sparse+dense hybrid; do they want us to replicate that or propose a Redwood-hosted solution?

Action items:
- Karthik: prepare SDK examples for both hosted auth (short-lived tokens) and private mTLS (sample config + cert rotation notes).
- Ben: confirm contract runway / pilot billing terms for a 5M ingest.
- Evelyn: prepare a one-page success criteria for pilot (latency targets, recall delta, cost threshold).

Thanks — I’ll own scheduling and customer comms.

Vanessa
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2027 10:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ACME pilot scope — tech clarifications and recommended migration approach

Thanks Vanessa — plan looks good. Quick tech confirmations and a short checklist I’ll bring to the QA call: 

1) SDK/auth examples: will provide Node + Python snippets. Hosted: bearer token flow using short-lived JWT from Console; Private: client cert + TLS mutual auth example.

2) Batching & memory knobs: start 128 vectors/batch, max 256. If customers use variable-length vectors in the future we’ll add padding/truncation guidance.

3) Normalization: we’ll treat their CSV as already L2-normalized. Our ingest path will check vector norm and warn on large deviations. If they switch embedding model (to 768) we’ll store both dims in separate indexes and set up a dual-query wrapper.

4) Reranker integration: plan to support two modes during pilot: Hosted cross-encoder for top-K (K=100), and a webhook to their on-prem reranker that accepts candidate IDs + payload.

5) Migration script: draft pseudo-workflow I’ll bring to call:
  - export_batch -> transform (if needed) -> POST /v1/embeddings/bulk?batch_size=128 -> verify ingest -> kick off indexing job -> sample recall test vs gold set -> mark pilot complete

I’ll attach the SDK examples and a short CLI tool in the meeting notes.

Karthik
Platform Engineering, Redwood Inference
